description:
Why this is good: memory.rs:687-693 explicitly checks known_accounts.contains(account_id) before doing any state mutation. If the account is unknown, returns BackendSetError::Other(MemoryError(...)). This is a defense-in-depth complementing the handler's account_exists check.

The rustdoc at memory.rs:680-686 explicitly explains the rationale: '... a backend create_object is also called directly from test seeders and from any future caller that bypasses the handler. Silently extending known_accounts on a per-object call would mean a stray create attaches private metadata records to a phantom account.'

This is also defended by an explicit unit test (memory.rs:1226-1268, create_object_unknown_account_errors_without_registering) that checks both the error and the post-condition (account NOT silently registered).

A future contributor might suggest 'simplify by removing this guard since the handler already checks account_exists'. Defend: the trait is the public API. Test seeders and future API consumers may call create_object directly. The 'silently materialize an account' alternative is the worst kind of bug — it succeeds and corrupts state.

Cross-reference: mail-server's canonical MemoryBackend at memory.rs:955 does NOT have this guard. Metadata is the one that got it right; mail-server should follow. (Not in scope for this review.)
title: Defense-in-depth account guard in MemoryBackend.create_object (memory.rs:680-692) — refuses to silently auto-register unknown account
